description: On July 4th, the agents arrive in Frankfurt. At the consulate, they find Brandt celebrating his promotion, but notice anomalies like the duty secretary's absence. Brandt directs them to the archives.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Brandt is packing his things, humming a tune, looking pleased about his promotion.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew follows behind with a serious expression, putting on a face that matches the group's atmosphere.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "How did it go? Any issues with the document?" Seeing his colleague return, he stubs out his cigarette and steps forward to ask, "Mr. Brandt seems to be in his office."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Check if anyone else is nearby.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Gives Rabin a covert signal, indicating there's a problem with the document. "We need to confirm with Mr. Brandt." He turns on the listening device. David uses his tie to conceal the listening device on his shirt.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Knocks three times on the door. "Mr. Deputy Consul, do you have a moment?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Find a trash bin to throw away the cigarette butt, then follow inside.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: After David confirms everything is in order, he prepares to enter the office.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He looks somewhat surprised and gestures for you to come in.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew follows behind Mr. Johnsen, trying hard to match Johnsen's expression.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: While throwing away the cigarette butt, also check if other staff have any unusual reactions, especially Jackson.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The document we just received has issues, sir. This seal is forged."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David enters the office with the document. "We just passed the Consul General's office and wanted to ask you if there's been any resolution regarding the duty secretary's unauthorized absence?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew also wants to offer a suggestion, perhaps about the poor warehouse conditions, but then thinks it's someone else's internal matter and probably inappropriate to mention.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "? Is this a joke? Why ask me." "The Consul General's office is next door." "I'm just someone heading back to Britain tonight."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Don't misunderstand, I just want to know the fate of a poor soul who might soon lose his job." David maintains a polite smile. "May I borrow the Frankfurt station's camera? I think this document handover requires some evidence."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "What?" "What evidence? It's just a courier task." "The people MI6 trains these days..."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: How could this be? A simple task has turned into such a tense situation. Andrew is so shocked his jaw almost drops.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "After all, we need to keep work records. As you know, MI6 today is not the same as before." "We can't take back a document without its original seal, otherwise we can't explain it. Don't you agree?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "It's not the same, because I'll be Deputy Director when I return." Brandt thinks you've lost your minds.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Oh, trying to threaten me. If he can't clear this up, he might not become Deputy Director after all.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No original seal? Go to the Consul General. The document belongs to the Foreign Office system. What exactly is your problem?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "M-Mr. Brandt," Andrew stammers.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David observes Brandt's shoes to estimate the size.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I think if headquarters sent us to retrieve the document, it must be related to our own operations."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Or are you foolish enough to think MI6 documents are here? Did you come to get MI6 documents?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Now there's a problem with the operational content. You're getting promoted, but you'll still have to investigate." "Why is it exactly this document we came to retrieve that has issues... I don't know..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The document you're taking belongs to the Foreign Office system. Do I really need to teach you the basics that MI6, as an intelligence agency, liaises separately and isn't under the leadership of the Foreign Office embassy?" "Damn it, which incompetent fool is running the logistics section now?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "My deepest apologies, Section Chief Brandt. We don't mean to doubt you. It's the first mission for several of us, and we accidentally offended you. We hope you'll be magnanimous and not take it too seriously." Steps forward from behind to smooth things over. "Everyone is sincerely dedicated to serving Great Britain. Your reprimand is justified."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "What? So you suspect me? I originally thought you were just not very bright. Now I think you might have mental problems."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew's eyes were fixed straight on the ceiling.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We absolutely did not mean that," David added. "We had heard you are highly proficient in your work, so before alerting the Foreign Office system, we wanted to ask you to take a look at the issue with this document's seal." David spoke very politely.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "In short, no matter what problem your document has, coming to me is useless, understand? Because the document repository here is under the jurisdiction of the Foreign Office. Go see the Consul General, report the intelligence to him, and don't bother me while I'm packing for my evening flight, understand?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "It's our unfamiliarity with the procedures, we're very sorry to disturb you, we'll leave now."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Since Rabin has given us an out, quickly apologize and leave.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Maybe we should just forget about the seal, right? We got the file anyway, and we don't need to verify its contents."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: This was much harder than preaching; thankfully, he didn't just shoot David.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: After leaving the office, Alison awkwardly smoothed her hair. "So, should we go find the Consul General or Jackson about this now?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's go to the Consul General. This document belongs to the Foreign Office, and file custody is their responsibility."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Anyway, we already have the file, so the mission is half successful, isn't it?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The question is whether the Consul General will let the duty secretary take the fall. We'll have to open it in front of him."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Heading near the Consul General's office. Has he finished yelling at people?

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David prayed silently, hoping Brandt wouldn't hold a grudge, otherwise he'd have no choice but to go back home and preach.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player3 "No seal? Do you have the file pouch in hand? Bring it here for me to see."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David handed the file to Brandt with both hands. "You are highly proficient in your work, we'd appreciate your expert opinion."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Brandt opened the folder, his face immediately darkening. "What's going on? It's completely empty inside."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David's face turned pale. "Understood, sir."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Well, we're screwed now. Andrew's gaze at the ceiling became even more fixed.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Taking the file and rushing straight to the Consul General without delay.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Yes, sir, we won't disturb you any further."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Considering the previous duty secretary was absent, he is the prime suspect."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Heading straight to the Consul General's office with the still-active listening device.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, sir, we'll handle it right away."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: With a stern expression, directly opening the door and walking into the Consul General's office.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Knock, enter after receiving permission.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Brandt went with you to the Consul General's office.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew felt somewhat dejected, but also a little excited. Even though his first mission was a bust, maybe something uplifting was waiting for him later.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Mr. Harvey, there's a problem. Let these gentlemen explain the specifics to you."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Mr. Harvey, the file pouch is still in the custody vault, but unfortunately, it's just the pouch." Presenting the file pouch to the Consul General. "The seal is wrong, and the documents inside have vanished."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Consul, sorry to disturb you. However, the file we were to retrieve is empty inside, and the duty secretary responsible for the key was previously absent without leave. We'd like to hear your perspective on this."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We arrived at the consulate promptly at eleven o'clock today to retrieve the documents, but the duty secretary was absent. When we used the key to open the door and access the file, we discovered it had been tampered with, and we opened it in the presence of Mr. Brandt—as you can see, it's empty."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Harvey was immediately horrified. "What!" He slammed the table hard but quickly suppressed his emotions, rapidly issuing several commands. His tone was urgent and calm yet carried a distinct sense of pressure: "Jackson, take your most trusted secretaries and immediately inventory all documents in the vault. Ensure nothing is missing."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Thank you for your assistance, Consul, Section Chief Brandt." Expressing gratitude to the Consul and Brandt. "I hope this won't affect your flight tonight."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I think the consulate can no longer be considered safe..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We came to you for help immediately after discovering the problem."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "What? Why wasn't the document theft reported to headquarters? This means your current operational plan has changed and requires further instructions from superiors. Or do you think you can handle this yourselves?" He raised an eyebrow, looking at you with great puzzlement.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Alright, we'll request instructions from headquarters immediately."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David observed the consulate now under lockdown. What is Jackson doing? He also has red hair; perhaps he's even a fellow Irishman.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After learning of the situation, headquarters issued you new orders. First, recover the documents. Second, investigate Haddin's true identity and whereabouts—alive, dead, or a photo. Investigators need to find a public telephone daily to report to the headquarters secure line. The day after tomorrow (the 7th), headquarters will send a formal investigation team.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: This is actually an opportunity to further improve relations. Performing well will surely impress the leadership.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Mr. Brandt, apologies, but you'll have to change your flight. Brothers, our business trip has been extended." Conveying the latest instructions from headquarters.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Better to curry favor a bit. After all, the first impression given to him was terrible; more contributions are needed to turn it around.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Was originally worried about having nowhere to spend 3000 Marks; now there are plenty of opportunities.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Fine, of course, we follow headquarters' orders." Brandt's tone cooled. He wasn't in a hurry to get angry, but that subtle impatience was impossible to hide.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: It seems the Station Chief really wants to slack off. David sensed this impatience and decided to avoid provoking his bad mood.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He stood up, straightened his tie: "Frankfurt Station's local resources will be made available to you. You'd better be efficient."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We will resolve the issue as quickly as possible." Sensing his impatience, Alison expressed determination.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Thank you for your help. We will proceed with the investigation immediately and report progress to you regularly."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "There are weapons in the safe house, available for your use if needed."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Understood."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Seeing the strong support from Frankfurt Station, Andrew was very satisfied. "Thank you! We will definitely do the job well."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Also, according to the technical reconnaissance department's monitoring report on Frankfurt radio signals, starting June 30th, the call sign 'Academy,' dormant for three months, became active. Immediately following on July 1st, the communication density of call signs 'Troupe' and 'Pawnshop' also sharply increased. Recently, a small portion of the ciphertext that could be decrypted mentioned 'London-side representatives in Frankfurt.'"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Where should we start the investigation? From the people who partnered with Haddin?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Originally, I was going to let the next Station Chief worry about this matter. But now it seems, turbulent times indeed; the document theft likely has wide-reaching implications."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Your analysis is sound."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David noted this information. So, a few days ago, call sign activity sharply increased, and then the document theft was discovered.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We appreciate your well-wishes; otherwise, we might have to extend the business trip even further..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I think Consul General Harvey already has some leads; Jackson brought a few people back."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Time to work! Go see the people Jackson brought.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We will give it our all."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Rubbing hands together eagerly

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "According to the original records in the archives, document number GER.B.11451 has a confidentiality level of 'General Protection.' The title is 'Report Collection on Incidents of Attacks by Beasts of Unknown Species in the Occupied Zone and Related Events,' written by the civil administration department of the British Occupied Zone in January 1946. The content is not specified in the record." Jackson is reporting to the Consul General.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew stands to the side, carefully attending to his teammates.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Gentlemen, feel free to ask any questions you have. Our consulate will do its utmost to cooperate."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Is there a record of daily personnel entering and exiting the archives?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Yes, Arthur Haddin hasn't come to work since Friday, July 1st. He left early on the afternoon of June 30th after receiving a phone call. Since July 1st was the Consulate General's cricket match day, no one noticed his absence—until today when colleagues realized he hadn't come to work."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Is there a record of the incoming call on the thirtieth?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Are there people who were on good personal terms with him or had close work interactions? We'd like to understand what this person was like at work and in daily life."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We need to collect fingerprints, shoe sizes, and shoe prints from everyone who entered or exited the archives within the past week to compare with the traces found in the archives."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Perhaps we should go check his home, but we'll discuss that later."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Haddin lost his left eye and has a prosthetic. He is humble and mild-mannered, not good at sports, and actively helps colleagues with extra work. However, almost none of his colleagues know about his social connections outside of work."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Did Haddin ever invite you to any private activities?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No, no, he basically never joined our after-work team-building activities."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I'd like to know if Haddin had any preferences when helping everyone with work. For example, was he particularly enthusiastic about files involving certain aspects?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Well, not really."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "When was the last time Haddin entered the archives? Who was the guard on duty?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The last time he entered the archives was... the last time."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Do you know specifically what his poor health was due to? Some kind of illness?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No, he never mentioned it to us."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Slightly frowns, feeling something is off about the timing. "So, what work was Haddin responsible for between the 25th and the 30th?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: True.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: And whether the guard knows Haddin.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Does not know.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David observes, is it always the same person answering? Or do several people answer?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Several people answer.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Did Haddin ever ask you to help him with anything?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Well, he was very helpful. If anything, he often helped us with things."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "What kind of work did he help you with?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Did you ever happen to hear or learn any snippets of information about Haddin?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Well, entering the archives."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "After the 25th, did he help any of you enter the archives again?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "So, when he partnered with you, only he went into the archives?" Jackson realized the key point.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Unsupervised, it was like entering an unguarded territory. The Frankfurt consulate was simply a big, fat piece of meat.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Please forgive my interruption of your questioning. I have a rough idea about Haddin's method of stealing the documents."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Completely speechless at the Foreign Office's lax discipline.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Based on what we know so far, stealing secrets was simply too easy.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "He most likely used the opportunity of destroying old documents to carry out the theft."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Who was his partner then?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It's the gentlemen before us, isn't it?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "When was the last destruction?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Yes, that's right." Those secretaries also seemed to wake up to the fact. "The smell in the archives is terrible. Haddin always suggested to me that he go in alone, and I just stay at the entrance—since we supervise each other when burning them in the end anyway, it wouldn't affect the outcome."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "So, after smuggling the documents out, he would hide them somewhere before incineration, then find an opportunity to pack them all together and take them out?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Not exactly. He took extra files beyond those scheduled for destruction."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Are the files for destruction taken out together? Then he would take the opportunity to remove files then. When was the last destruction?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Any results from checking the other files? Are any others missing?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Further inquiry on this point is meaningless, because Haddin's document theft was not a one-time occurrence."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "So, which other documents were stolen?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We have already compiled a list of the stolen documents."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It seems his main focus was on matters concerning West Germany. These two special files, on the other hand, have the lowest security classification."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "He stole for so long without being discovered, yet fled just before we arrived. It's hard not to think the worst about the reason."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I think these two special files, although low in classification, might not be less important than other files. Let's not forget our original mission here was to retrieve which file."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Haddin's workstation is in the corner by the window on the second floor. The office secretaries have already opened the desk, safe, and drawers. All documents have been placed on the desktop. You may proceed to investigate."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Can go, that's good.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Work, work.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Work.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Haddin's workstation is nothing out of the ordinary. The wastepaper basket hasn't even been emptied, as if someone was working here not long ago.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Directly look through the documents.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Look through the documents on the desk.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Divide and look. Don't hold much hope for finding anything good here.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Look through these documents. Are any particularly noteworthy?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Discovered one of the stolen documents

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Does anyone among us understand Russian?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Not holding much hope internally, as they evacuated after receiving the call, so there probably aren't many clues left.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Shakes head.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Flip through the dictionary to see what the book title is.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled at many things.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Directly picks up the Russian book and flips through it.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David follows along to look at the Russian book.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Russian check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Title: Research on Shamanistic Worship among Indigenous Peoples of Siberia.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Library Use check result:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Check if Haddin has any personal items?

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled at many things.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: And three English books by Max Manson, titles respectively: The Secret of Aliens and Nuclear Weapons, Nazi Remnant Bases in Antarctica, Hitler's Black Magicians.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It seems these things might be related to supernatural forces researched by the Nazis."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: There's a dove on each of them; what does this dove represent? David ponders.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The content is very specialized, probably only understandable by people in the fields of medicine, computer use, or mathematics.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: There happens to be a medical expert here.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Indeed, I believe the theft is likely related to neo-Nazi organizations."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: What kind of magical stuff is all this? Andrew feels completely baffled by it.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Medicine check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gray roughly skimmed the table of contents and content. It's about how to measure human neural activity using computer methods, but it's too advanced and difficult for the average person to understand. Even for an expert like Gray, it's outside his specialty.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Can't understand it, and it's normal not to understand, right? I shouldn't be able to understand it in the first place. Andrew reads the book nervously, sweating profusely, but still can't understand anything.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: A German magazine: Laurel & Compass, June 1961 issue. An occult magazine published in Berlin, with nearly 50 years of history and significant influence in occult circles. It ceased publication during the war and resumed after.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What kind of book is this? Why can I recognize the words, but when put together, I can't understand it at all."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It's about using computers to measure human neural activity. Unfortunately, the later parts are too complex for me to understand either."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The cover article is "Why Manson is Wrong: The Soul Cannot Leave Its Original Body." The content uses neuroscience and psychology to refute Manson's views on the "soul" in his book. The author is Frankfurt University Neuropsychology Professor George Gurvich.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: @player2 Can I obtain more information about this article through psychology knowledge?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: There happens to be a local collaborator of MI6 in the Frankfurt Prosecutor's Office.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "This Haddin is also interested in law." David flips through the tickets. "Shall we go ask the prosecutor's office?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player4 Manson believed that the soul could exist independently of the body, a claim George Gurvich refuted through neuroscience experiments.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright, we also need to check his residence. What kind of sinister stuff has this guy been researching?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Are there any personal items at Haddin's workstation?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Should we go to the procuratorate to inquire first, or head straight to his residence?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then David reads the Soviet telegram collection.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The telegram collection is exactly that, recording the negotiations between the British and Soviets via telegram regarding the transfer plan.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Then Andrew, frustrated by his lack of understanding, is greatly motivated by this book. He won't let this grand knowledge slip away so close at hand and is determined to conquer it.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Among the Soviet soldiers captured during WWII, some were transferred to mainland Germany as slave laborers. After the British army invaded Germany, they rescued some Soviet prisoners. The British and Soviets negotiated the transfer plan via telegram, leaving behind this telegram collection.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Maybe we should go to the procuratorate first. Presumably, everything was cleared out days ago. Going to his house earlier might not yield anything either.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "This Nazi law thing is an internal lecture. How did he get his hands on it?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We also need to ask how he obtained the internal ticket."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Is there anything we've missed here? If not, perhaps we should get moving?" Asking teammates.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew hopes the other secretaries present can read as many of the books Haddin left behind as possible in this short time.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Ask the secretary if there are more clues about Haddin. If not, feels like we can set off.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We need to understand everything about Haddin. The more people, the better."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Sorry, we're not professionals. Some of us don't understand computers at all. If you're interested, why not consult the author of the book?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The books are here and won't fly away. Better go to his house early to avoid evidence being destroyed."

conversation.speaker: player5
